beats.narration_text: We give Claude a v0 sentence and ask it to generate a complete five-section SDD, then run the Principle Collision Test on all three architecture principles.

props.command:
v0: Local timeline editor — one user, browser-only, no backend.
Generate a five-section SDD:
  1. Problem Statement (one user, one done-condition)
  2. Architecture Principles (run Collision Test)
  3. User Needs (stopwatch-measurable)
  4. Component List (explicit non-components)
  5. Open Questions

beats.narration_text: Claude generates the five sections. The Collision Test flags a conflict between local-only and any future sync requirement. The non-component list explicitly names: no backend, no database, no login.

props.title: sdd.md
props.code:
# SDD - Local Timeline Editor

## 1. Problem Statement
One user edits a personal timeline in the browser.
Done when: user can add, reorder, and delete events
without losing data across page refreshes.

## 2. Architecture Principles
- Local-only [COLLISION: conflicts with sync]
- localStorage only [COLLISION: conflicts with multi-device]
- No external deps [COLLISION: conflicts with rich UI libs]

## 4. Component List
IN:  EventList, EventEditor, LocalStorageAdapter
OUT: backend, database, login, sync, sharing

artifactLines: Five sections: Problem Statement, Architecture Principles, User Needs, Component List, Open Questions.
The Principle Collision Test flags conflicts between principles before code is written.
The non-component list names what the system will NOT do — no backend, no database, no login.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Pick your next side project. Before any code, write a five-section SDD: Problem Statement with one user and one done-condition, Architecture Principles each run through the Collision Test, User Needs measured with a stopwatch, a Component List that names its explicit non-components, and the Open Questions you have not answered yet. Then flag the principle that survives the fewest realistic conflicts — that is the one that would have drifted first.

props.topic: YOUR TURN · CLAUDE CODE FOR STUDENTS
props.command:
Pick your next side project. Before any code is written, produce a five-section SDD:
  1. Problem Statement — one user, one done-condition.
  2. Architecture Principles — run the Collision Test on each principle explicitly.
  3. User Needs — every one stopwatch-measurable.
  4. Component List — name at least three explicit non-components.
  5. Open Questions.
Then flag the ONE principle most likely to fail the Collision Test if the scope grows.
